sentences.text:
Author: Sanjay Kumar Bench: Sanjay Kumar  1  IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA  CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION  CRIMINAL APPEAL NO. OF 2024  (arising out of SLP (Crl.) No. 6996 of 2024)
 HARINDER SAH APP  VERSUS  STATE OF BIHAR AND ANOTHER ..... RESP
O R D E R Leave granted.
Our attention is drawn to the victims statement under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
Referring to the statement of the victim, it is argued that the disputes pertain to the share of the victim in the property on account of the death of her husband.

No doubt, the father of the victim had made personal allegations against the appellant, Harinder Sah, but on being questioned by the Court, had stated that if the victim gets her share, there would be no dispute.
The appellant, Harinder Sah, was granted interim protection by this Court, vide order dated 21.05.2024.

Keeping in view the facts and circumstances of the case, we accept the present appeal and direct that in the event of the appellant, Complaint Case No. 515 of 2020 for the offence(s) punishable under Sections 354B and 498A of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, he shall be released on bail by the arresting/investigating officer/trial court on terms and conditions to be fixed by the trial court.
In addition, the appellant, Harinder Sah, shall comply with the conditions mentioned in Section 438(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
Recording the aforesaid, the impugned order is set aside and the appeal is allowed.
